newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 25.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Record turnover of 34.6 billion drachmas at the Athens bourse yesterday as the general price index powered forward another 2.55 percent, closing at 1,366.92 units. The surge in volume is considered to be a direct result of the continuing downward trend in inflation and interest rates and, subsequent lesser returns from state titles.
--New computer programs at the finance ministry will allow officials to cross-check data on rentals and income and ownership of yachts and other luxury items.
--The Agricultural Bank of Greece is hoping for more than 20 billion drachmas in the sale of part of its majority share in the Bank of Central Greece.

--Greece's telecoms organisation, OTE, and the national economy and finance ministry are torn between two scenarios for OTE's second flotation. Common ground, however, has been found on the details: some 67 million shares at a price of 5,500 drachmas will bring OTE an estimated 370 billion drachmas.

--The barrage of interest rate cuts on deposits and state titles late last week received the Athens bourse's response yesterday when investors went searching for better returns. Demand for constructions and investment led the rally.

--Deputy Finance Minister George Drys yesterday extended the deadline for tax declarations by 10 days, following problems on how to complete the E9 real estate declaration and delays in sending out tax forms following strike action at the ministry's services.
--There's intense interest from the European Union in financing the Stavros-Elefsina road axis with discussions on including it in a special programme.
--Mitsubishi Bank has protested over the state's failure to provide guarantees for its 30 billion drachma loan to the Greek Railways Organisation, OSE.

--A recent study has revealed that Greek banks can expect a significant change in market share and profits over the next few years. The study will be presented today at a conference on profit-making strategies for banks.
--The finance ministry will cut interest rates on its new issue of treasury bills by 0.40 percent, in line with an expected drop in February inflation to 6.6 percent.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said yesterday that 1997 was a year of "real changes" in the economy and called on the business world to support them with investments. Papandoniou said the difference in interest rates between deposits and lending would be rationalised and that the lack of competitiveness between Greek banks was a problem.
--The second OTE flotation will probably take place in May, according to sources at OTE and the national economy ministry.

--The Athens bourse is proceeding with the establishment of new bodies and mechanisms that will guarantee its upgraded operation, including a new code of condust which will come into effect in the first half-year and modernisation of computer systems which will assist in the creation of new financial products. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
